sampling_model.design: Randomized binary treatment with known allocation probability \(\pi\in[\pi_0,1-\pi_0]\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of \(O=(A,X,Y)\) from the observed Gaussian law \(P_{\vartheta}\) indexed by \(\vartheta\in\Theta\); ordinary Wald inference is restricted to \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\), while projection inference and the angular frontier retain their stated whole-class domains.
sampling_model.overlap: The allocation probability is uniformly separated from zero and one.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-dimensional map \(\theta(P)\) is estimated from arm-specific means, variances, and outcome-covariances and the pooled covariate covariance on an evaluation split independent of covariate selection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The underlying conditional-optimal-transport information model requires a shared covariate marginal and motivates variable selection; compact-support assumptions used by particular published theorems do not themselves cover the Gaussian frontier class.
Sparse covariance eigenvalues lower-bound the regression submodularity ratio and yield a forward-selection approximation guarantee.
Submodularity ratio and generalized curvature jointly yield a tight generic cardinality-constrained greedy guarantee.
Multiplier-bootstrap aggregation permits valid covariate and model selection among conditional-transport dual bounds.
A smooth-density quadratic conditional-transport estimator has a fixed-target central limit theorem away from equality.
A short never-empty confidence interval is valid when estimated lower and upper bounds have a regular joint Gaussian limit.

body.tldr: For a randomized Gaussian experiment, retaining pretreatment covariates raises the information-specific conditional-optimal-transport lower endpoint for the mean squared individual treatment effect. Each increment is a squared chordal distance between upper-hemisphere residual-score lifts. A sharp diagonal-normalization lemma and a spherical midpoint--tangent argument give the exact fixed-budget frontier \(\rho_k(K,R)=k/[1+(k-1)KR]\) for \(k\ge2\) and \(R>1\), with \(\rho_k=1\) when \(k=1\) or \(R=1\). The unequal-scale Gaussian family approaches this value, and its large-budget limit \(1/(KR)\) is the exact dimension-free frontier. Forward greedy inherits the corresponding exact finite-budget factor. Independent evaluation yields credited conditional Wald inference on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) and a conservative raw-moment projection interval on all of \(\Theta\), including equality. The Gaussian class lies inside Lin et al.'s underlying common-marginal COT information model, but neither the Gaussian lower theorem nor its adverse converse is asserted for that paper's compact-support theorem class without a separate approximation argument.

project_justification.gap: Conditional optimal transport supplies sharp covariate-assisted causal bounds, but existing work treats the conditioning set as fixed. Generic weak-submodularity theory does not determine the finite-budget approximation ratio of the unequal-scale two-arm Gaussian endpoint, and the earlier separate frame and hemisphere comparisons leave a strict finite-\(k\) gap.
project_justification.niche: The Gaussian endpoint has a residual-score geometry that is absent from one-response regression: singleton and joint gains are chordal distances observed through a sparse Schur-complement frame.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the residual-score chordal geometry, proves the exact fixed-budget frontier \(k/[1+(k-1)KR]\) with its \(k=1\) and \(R=1\) elbows, realizes the frontier by fully randomized unequal-scale Gaussian laws, takes its exact dimension-free limit, transfers the finite-budget value to greedy selection, and formulates credited sample-split Wald and whole-class projection inference.

body.related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2025) introduce covariate-assisted conditional transport, establish fixed-information results, give Gaussian benchmarks, and identify variable selection as future work. The present Gaussian classes are contained in their underlying common-marginal COT information model. This inclusion does not place Gaussian laws inside the compact-support and regularity class used by particular published sharpness or estimation theorems: the Gaussian lower bound is proved directly here, and the adverse Gaussian converse transfers only to superclasses that actually contain these laws, absent a separate truncation or approximation theorem. Das and Kempe (2011), Bian et al. (2017), and Elenberg et al. (2018) supply generic weak-submodularity and greedy machinery; they do not give the two-arm angular frontier. Ji, Lei, and Spector (2023) already supply selection-valid conditional-transport inference, so post-selection validity is credited rather than claimed as novel. Lin et al. (2026) provide fixed-target smooth-density inference, and Stoye (2021) motivates conservative boundary-robust projection; neither comparator supplies the exact covariate-budget frontier.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The extremal laws approach the exact ratio through a positive but vanishing endpoint contrast as \(h\downarrow0\). This is sufficient for the infimum defining the submodularity frontier, but it does not establish that the generic greedy value factor is itself worst-case sharp at a fixed signal amplitude. The exact theorem is Gaussian and does not transfer its lower bound to the broader model-lean information class. Conversely, the adverse Gaussian family transfers only to a superclass containing these Gaussian laws, not literally to a compact-support theorem class without a proved truncation or approximation argument. Ordinary Wald inference is asserted only on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\); equality laws have zero first-order endpoint variance and are handled by whole-image projection. Computing optimal sparse margins may be combinatorial, so certified \(m,M,s,V\) remain inputs.
body.honest_scope: The exact fixed-budget frontier, its \(k=1\) and \(R=1\) elbows, its dimension-free limit, and the induced greedy guarantee are proved over the explicitly quantified randomized Gaussian sparse-margin classes. The extremal construction specifies the covariate distribution, independent arm noises, independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment, potential outcomes, and observed outcome. The Gaussian class is a subclass of Lin et al.'s underlying common-marginal COT information model only; no claim is made that the Gaussian lower theorem holds over the broader model-lean class or that the Gaussian converse lies inside a compact-support theorem class. Sample-split Wald coverage on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) and conservative projection coverage on all of \(\Theta\), including equality, are credited finite-dimensional inference specializations rather than novelty claims. No locally shortest equality-boundary interval, robustness theorem for Gaussian misspecification, polynomial-time sparse-margin certification, or worst-case sharpness of the generic greedy recurrence is claimed.
body.interpretation: For \(k\ge2\) and \(R>1\), the best law-uniform submodularity certificate at the stated sparse margins is \(k/[1+(k-1)KR]\), not merely \(1/(KR)\). The gain is material at small budgets and vanishes continuously toward the exact dimension-free limit as \(k\to\infty\). When \(k=1\), the only eligible comparison is a singleton and the ratio is one. When \(R=1\), the variance ceiling and residual floor force all covariate--outcome covariances to vanish, so \(F\equiv0\) and the convention again returns one.
